                     <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Act. 3.13.</ns0:note> And shall deliver him to the Gentiles, to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi>: and the third day he shall rise again.<ns0:note place="bottom">Both <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> give us account of this Passage. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith Chap. 10.32. <ns0:hi>And they were in the way going up <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>o Hierusalem, Iesus went before them, and they were amazed, and as they followed, they were afraid, and he took again the twelve, and began again to tell them, what things should happen unto him: Saying, behold we go up to Hierusalem, and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief Priests, and to the Scribes, and they shall condemn him to death, and deliver him to the Gentiles, and they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and spit upon him, and shall kill him, and the third day he shall rise again. Luke</ns0:hi> hath it Chap. 18.31. <ns0:hi>Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold we go up to Hierusalem, and all things that are written by the Prophets concerning the Son of man, shall be accomplished; for he shall be delivered to the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully intreated, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>d spit upon, and they shall scourge him, and put him to de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>h, and the third day he shall rise again. And they understood none of these things, and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>gs that were spoken.</ns0:hi> Our blessed Lord was yet upon his road from <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi>; we have here an account of some of his travelling Discourse, to teach us to make use of all time for edifying, and profitable Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, that as they went, <ns0:hi>Iesus went before them, and they were amazed, and as they followed they were afraid. Mark</ns0:hi> gives us no account of any formidable <ns0:hi>Object</ns0:hi> in their Eye: Those that think they were <ns0:hi>amazed</ns0:hi> to see him make such hast to his death, forget that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, that af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter our Savior had further instructed them in this, <ns0:hi>they under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood it not</ns0:hi>; But probably they knew he was going into the Nest of his Enemies, and this made them afraid. He calls to him the twelve, (it was not a Discourse fit for a Multitude) and gives them an Account very particularly of what he had twice or thrice before taught them; he had before told them of his Death and Resurrection, and that he should be <ns0:hi>betray<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to death</ns0:hi>; here he describes the manner, <ns0:hi>they should deliver him to the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> (to <ns0:hi>Pilate</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi>) he describes his previous Sufferings, he should be <ns0:hi>scourged, mocked, spit upon,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the kind of his Death,</ns0:hi> he should be <ns0:hi>crucified</ns0:hi>; that when these things came to pass, they might be assured that he was God, who had so punctually foretold things to come, not ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />istent in their causes, but meer Contingencies, he comforteth them with two things. 1. <ns0:hi>That it was according to what had been foretold by the Prophets.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>That tho he died, he should rise again the third Day.</ns0:hi> They had need of this fore-warn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, for a fore-arming; for considering that they now looked upon him as <ns0:hi>the Messiah,</ns0:hi> it might well pose them to think how he should dy; and when they had seen all these things come to pass, it might have shaken their Faith, but being so particularly foretold, the coming of them to pass, rather con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firmed their Faith in him as the Son of God, than weakened it. But <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>They understood none of these things,</ns0:hi> That is, surely they <ns0:hi>believed</ns0:hi> none of them, the <ns0:hi>Saying was hid from them.</ns0:hi> The words were plain enough, but they could not reconcile them to their Reason, they could not conceive how he who was the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> could die: nor get over the Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />judice of his being a <ns0:hi>temporal Prince,</ns0:hi> and exercising a King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom in this World: For his <ns0:hi>rising again the third Day,</ns0:hi> they could not believe it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:255" />20 Then came to him the mother of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.21.</ns0:note> Ze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bedees children with her Sons, worshipping <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and desiring a certain thing of him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And he saith unto her, What wilt thou? She saith unto him, Grant that these my two Sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other the left, in thy Kingdom.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith Chap. 10.35. And <ns0:hi>Iames, and Iohn, the Son, of Zebedee, came unto him saying, Master, we would that thou should do for us what we desire. And he said, what would you, that I should do for you? They said unto him, Grant unto us, that we may sit, one on thy right Hand, the other on thy left Hand in thy Glory. Matthew</ns0:hi>'s saying, <ns0:hi>In thy Kingdom, Mark,</ns0:hi> In thy Glory, leaves us in some doubt whether these two Disciples and their Mother, had here some carnal Notion of the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Heaven,</ns0:hi> because Christ had before spoken of some that should be first in it, and others last. Or were in some expectation of some glorious secular Kingdom, which Christ after his Resurrection should exercise in the World; for that they had some such Thoughts, appears from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 22.24. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.6. This Mother of <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>Salome Mark.</ns0:hi> 15.40. A constant follower of Christ, <ns0:hi>Mat</ns0:hi> 27.55, 56. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith she spake, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith her two Sons spake. They would first have had a general Grant from Christ of <ns0:hi>whatsoever they should ask,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>certain thing.</ns0:hi> But wise Men use not to grant such Requests; Our Lord askes them what they would desire? Then do they betray their Ambiti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on. Was there ever a more unseasonable Request, than for them to be Suitors for great Places to him, when he had but now told them, he was going to be <ns0:hi>Spit upon, Scourged, Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demned, Crucified?</ns0:hi> Yet there was this good in it, they by it discovered a Faith in him, that notwithstanding all this, he should be exalted, and have a Kingdom. But how carnal are our Conceptions of Spiritual and Heavenly Things, till we be taught of God a right Notion of them?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye aske. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the Baptisme, that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.38, 39. Our Savior gently reproves them for their inadvised Petition, and again mindeth them, that he <ns0:hi>was first to Suffer, and then to enter into his glory,</ns0:hi> and that by much Tribulation they also must enter in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to the Kingdom of God, which was a thing fitter for their present Thoughts, than sitting at his <ns0:hi>right hand,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>left hand,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>we must suffer with him, if we will be glorified together,</ns0:hi> Rom. 8.17. <ns0:hi>How ready are</ns0:hi> we to ask we know not what? <ns0:hi>Are you able to drink of the Cup,</ns0:hi> &c. The Sence is, are you able to Suffer, what I am to Suffer? Hereby our Savior intimates, That those who are the freest, and greatest Sufferers for Christ: shall have the greatest Rewards from him. Christ here expresseth his Sufferings under the Notion of <ns0:hi>Drinking of a Cup, and being Baptised with a Baptism. A Cup</ns0:hi> is an ordinary Metaphor in Holy Writ, by which a M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ns Portion in this Life is expressed, whither it be a Portion of good Things or evil. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 11.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>6 <ns0:hi>Isai.</ns0:hi> 51.17. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 25.15. <ns0:hi>Lam.</ns0:hi> 4.21. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 26.39, 40, 42. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 18.11. Drinking of a Cup is usu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally put for Suffering <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 49.12. <ns0:hi>Ezech.</ns0:hi> 23.32. <ns0:hi>Obad.</ns0:hi> 16. The <ns0:hi>Metaphor</ns0:hi> being as some think, taken from a Custom in some Nations, to put Malefactors to Death by giving them <ns0:hi>a Cup of Poyson to drink,</ns0:hi> or as others think, from the leud Custome, at compotations to force men to drink off their Cups. To <ns0:hi>be Baptized with the Baptisme I am Baptized with,</ns0:hi> hath the same Import, see <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 12.50. Afflictions are ordinarily compared in Scripture to <ns0:hi>Waters</ns0:hi>: To be <ns0:hi>Baptized,</ns0:hi> is to be dipped in Water; <ns0:hi>Metaphorically</ns0:hi> to be plunged in Af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flictions: I am saith Christ to be <ns0:hi>baptized with B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ood,</ns0:hi> over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />whelmed with Sufferings and Afflictions, Are you able to be so? <ns0:hi>They say unto him, we are able.</ns0:hi> This was as rashly spoke as the other. How little do we know our own Strength? <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 26.56. When Christ was apprehended, <ns0:hi>they all forsook him and fled.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And he saith unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of my cup, and be baptized with the bap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tisme that I am baptized with, but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, ‖ is not mine <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 25.34.</ns0:note> to give, but <ns0:hi>it shall be given to them</ns0:hi> for whom it is prepared of my Father.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.39, 40. Our Savior here tells them, that as he was first to Suffer and then enter into his Glory; so they that should be glorified with him, should also first suffer with him, for none shall be Crowned, but those who strive Lawfully, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.5. And all that will live Godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer Persecution, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.12. But who should be highest in the Kingdom of Glory, his Father must determine upon <ns0:hi>whose Will,</ns0:hi> the disposal of his Kingdom, and the preferences in it depended. This Text hath been abused, by those who have denied Christ's <ns0:hi>Deity,</ns0:hi> and Equality to the Father, as if it served their Purpose: Because Christ here denieth it in his Power, to dispose of the Kingdom of Heaven; but besides that, he elsewhere asserts the contrary. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 10.28. & 17.2<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Christ doth not here speak of what was in his Power but what was his Office as Mediator, so his work was to in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courage them to fight the good Fight, not to dispense out Crowns to them. Or else, he speaketh of himself as Man, as he speaketh, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 14.28. Nor indeed doth Christ here deny, that it was in his Power, but only that it was in his Power, to give this preference to any, except those for whom his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther had prepared it: Note the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> is, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, That is, <ns0:hi>Is not mine to give, but to them for whom it is prepared</ns0:hi>: So that those words [<ns0:hi>it shall be given to them</ns0:hi>] which our Translators put in, were better left out. All this was before ordered and determined by God, and he could only dispose of the Kingdom of God, according to the Eternal Council, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> (which we translate <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi>) hath here the Force of <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> (unless) as in <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 9.8. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.5. Besides that to shew the Order of the <ns0:hi>Trinity</ns0:hi> in working; <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Providence,</ns0:hi> are usually ascribed to the <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> tho by other Scriptures it appears, that the <ns0:hi>Son</ns0:hi> in them co-operateth with the Father.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 22.24<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>25.</ns0:note> And when the ten heard <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they were moved with indignation against the two brethren.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 10.41. Here is not yet a Word of <ns0:hi>Peters Prima<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cy,</ns0:hi> or any Claim he put in for it, nor it seemeth, had the others any Apprehension of such an E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ablishment, for then, neither would <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> have put in <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or it, nor would all the Disciples (among whom <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was one) have been so displea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed at the Ambition of <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> yet they seem to be sick of the same Disease, and to have been displeased only, that they had the start of the Motion, and had put in their Petition first.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles, exer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Pet. 5.3.</ns0:note> it shall not be so amongst you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 23.11. Mar. 9.35.</ns0:note> but whosoever will be great amongst you, let him be your minister.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And whosoever will be chief amongst you, let him be your servant.<ns0:note place="bottom">So <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath much the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.42, 43, 44. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath also much the same, (but it seemeth spoken at another time) <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 22.25, 26, 27. I shall not here inter-meddle with the Disputes, some have founded on this Text: <ns0:hi>Whether there may be a Civil Magistracy amongst Christians</ns0:hi>: A thing undoubt<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />edly Foreign to the Sense of this Text. Or, <ns0:hi>Whether Christ here Establisheth a Party amongst Ministers</ns0:hi>; Which I do not think our Lords design here: Nor yet, with that other Question, <ns0:hi>Whether Ministers of the Gospel may take upon them, the exercise of any Civil Power.</ns0:hi> That which our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour here intendeth, 1. <ns0:hi>To distinguish his Kingdom from the Kingdoms of the World</ns0:hi>: Those Kingdoms are over mens Bodies and Estates, his was a <ns0:hi>spiritual Kingdom,</ns0:hi> over the Hearts and Consciences of Men. Or rather, his was a <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Glory,</ns0:hi> where there would be no need of <ns0:hi>Ru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lers</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Magistrates,</ns0:hi> as in the Governments of the World, nor any such Exercise of Authority, as is here Exercised in the Government of Earthly Kingdoms, and <ns0:hi>Policies.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>To condemn Ambition, and Pride in his Disciples,</ns0:hi> as making them most unfit for this Kingdom, which is a thing he had before taught them. The way to be greatest in Heaven, is to be humblest, to be Low, and mean in our own Eyes: This I think to be the Properest Interpretation of this Text, Our Lord by it Correcting the Erroneous Opinion his Disciples had of the Nature of his Kingdom, as also their <ns0:hi>Pride</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ambition,</ns0:hi> and pressing upon them other Studies, than how to be the greate<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t in any Earthly Kingdom. If any do think, that in this Text our Lord hath some respect to the Kingdom he hath upon Earth. He rather Checks <ns0:hi>Ambition,</ns0:hi> and an <ns0:hi>Affectation of Superiority,</ns0:hi> than any thing else, and lets us know, that such as <ns0:hi>Love the Preheminence</ns0:hi> are most unfit for it: That the work of Heads of the Church, is but a <ns0:hi>Ministry,</ns0:hi> not a <ns0:hi>Domination,</ns0:hi> and that those who are fittest for it, and deserve most Honour in the Church; are those that least seek and affect it: And those most unworthy of that Honour, who most hunt after it. But I prefer the first Sense, given of this Text. For certainly, what our Saviour here saith, was not only occasioned by, but had a great Relation to the Petition of <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> with their Mother; and the bearing Rule, and exercising Authority mentioned here, relates to the <ns0:hi>King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom,</ns0:hi> mentioned in that Petition. Which I think cannot be understood of the <ns0:hi>Church,</ns0:hi> which was a Kingdom of Christ; which they as yet little understood, but they either meant the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Glory,</ns0:hi> intertaining carnal Conceptions of that, that there would be some Superiority, and Inferiority there amongst the Saints, which our Saviour here Correcteth their mistake in. Or, else they Fancied a secular Kingdom, to be Exercised by Christ on Earth, after his Resurrection from the Dead. Our Saviour Correcteth this mistake also, intimating that his Kingdom should be of another Nature, and the way to be highest in it, was to be <ns0:hi>Humble</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Low,</ns0:hi> and mean in Opinions of our selves.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:256" />28 Even as the Son of man came not to be mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stred unto, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 22.27. Joh. 13.14.</ns0:note> but to minister and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Tit. 2.14. 1 Pet 1.19.</ns0:note> to give his life a ransom for many.<ns0:note place="bottom">So saith <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.45. the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.7. he <ns0:hi>made himself of no Reputation, and took upon him the form of a Servant.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour had before taught them, that <ns0:hi>the Disciple is not above his Master.</ns0:hi> Such saith our Saviour, as is the <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> in my Kingdom, such must the Rulers and great Persons in it be: See what a Kingdom I have, I came not to be Ministred unto, but to <ns0:hi>Minister,</ns0:hi> to serve the Necessities of Men and Womens Souls and Bodies: And to <ns0:hi>give my Life a ransom for many,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> a <ns0:hi>Redemption price</ns0:hi>; the Apostle useth <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which signifieth a Price paid in stead of another, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.6. So as there is no further <ns0:hi>Satis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />faction,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Price</ns0:hi> to be paid for any.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And as they departed from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And behold two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus passed by, cryed saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou son of David.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace, but they cryed the more, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou son of David.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, what will ye, that I shall do unto you?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 They say unto him, Lord! that our eyes may be opened.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 So Jesus had compassion on them, and touch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed their eyes and immediately their eyes received sight, and they followed him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> repeateth the same Story, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10. from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 46. to the end with several more Circumstances, 1. He mentioneth only <ns0:hi>one Blind man,</ns0:hi> and nameth him <ns0:hi>Bartimeus</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Time<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />us.</ns0:hi> He saith, the Blind man was <ns0:hi>Begging, Mark</ns0:hi> saith, when Christ called the Blind man, they said unto him. <ns0:hi>Be of good Comfort, rise, he calleth thee. And he casting away his Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, rose and came to Iesus.</ns0:hi> He further adds, that Christ said to him. <ns0:hi>Go thy way, thy Faith hath made thee whole, Luke</ns0:hi> relateth the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 18. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 35. to the end. He saith, <ns0:hi>As he was come nigh to Iericho,</ns0:hi> he mentioneth but <ns0:hi>one Blind man</ns0:hi>: In repeating Christ's words, he saith, <ns0:hi>Iesus saith unto him, receive thy sight, thy Faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, Glorifying God; and all the People when they saw it, gave Praise unto God.</ns0:hi> Our Lord presently gives his Disciples a Demonstration of what he had said. That he <ns0:hi>came to Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nister,</ns0:hi> to serve even the poorest, and most Despicable Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures. <ns0:hi>Iericho</ns0:hi> was a City not far from <ns0:hi>Iordan, Ios.</ns0:hi> 3.16. it was taken, <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 6. and upon the Division of the Land, fell within the Lot of <ns0:hi>Benjamen, Ios.</ns0:hi> 18.21. Our Saviour took it in his way from <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> Probably these Blind men, or <ns0:hi>Bartimeus</ns0:hi> at least, who alone is mentioned by <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> hearing Christ was coming, sate first on the side of <ns0:hi>Iericho</ns0:hi> next <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> and then got him on the other side, as our Saviour was leaving the Town. Which makes <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> say, <ns0:hi>as he came nigh,</ns0:hi> and the two other Evange<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lists say<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>as he went out of Iericho,</ns0:hi> he sate begging. <ns0:hi>Bar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />timeus</ns0:hi> (being as it should seem) the most known, and the most Famous, is alone mentioned by <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke, Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> (naming none) saith there were two. Which <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> deny not, but knowing only the Name of the one of them: They mention only one: They speak to our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour, under the Notion of the Son of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> by which they owned him as the true <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi>; for that was a Title by which the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> was known amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> according to the Prophecies of him. They ask him for <ns0:hi>Mercy,</ns0:hi> they continue in their Cry, tho the multitudes rebuked them, as possibly thinking, they only came to ask some <ns0:hi>Alms,</ns0:hi> and were too importunate, seeing our Lord seemed not to regard them. God sometimes tryeth our <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> (by delays) how it will hold out, but he never frustrateth it. This mindeth us of our Duty, to <ns0:hi>Pray without ceasing.</ns0:hi> Christs stops, calleth them, askes them what they would have? They seem most sensible of their Bodily wants, and Answer. <ns0:hi>Lord that our Eyes may be opened.</ns0:hi> Jesus hath Compassion on them, toucheth their Eyes, Christ sometimes, but not always in healing, touched the affected part, and (as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith) he said, <ns0:hi>Receive thy sight.</ns0:hi> The Miracle is wrought, they pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sently are able to see. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth, that Christ said, <ns0:hi>Thy Faith hath made thee whole</ns0:hi>; we have met with the same Phrase before. I <ns0:hi>have made thee whole,</ns0:hi> but thy <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in me, hath prevailed with me to do it. Their Faith in his Power was seen in their owning him, as the true <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi> So able to do it. 2. In their <ns0:hi>imploring his Mercy,</ns0:hi> and going on in their Cryes, of that Nature, tho they met with a <ns0:hi>Rebuke. Faith,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>fervent Prayer</ns0:hi> do great things with God, because of his Compassion. <ns0:hi>The Prayer of Faith shall save</ns0:hi> the sick, <ns0:hi>Iam.</ns0:hi> 5.15. <ns0:hi>& v.</ns0:hi> 16. <ns0:hi>The Effectual fervent Prayer of a righteous Man availeth much.</ns0:hi> Nor is any Man so mean, and Contemptible in the World (these two Blind men were Beggers) but if they can believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, if they will lye in Christ's way, if they will Cry unto him, and not give over their Crys; they shall obtain at our Saviours hands greater things than these. This Miracle gaineth God Glory from the multitude, and from the Blind man, not only <ns0:hi>Praise,</ns0:hi> but a Resolution to <ns0:hi>follow Christ.</ns0:hi> This should be the Effect of all Salvations wrought for us, Mercy is then duely improved, when it bringeth forth in our Hearts, Glory and Praise to God; and ingageth us, to follow the Lord Jesus Christ. Our Saviour had wrought his former Miracles in <ns0:hi>Ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lilee,</ns0:hi> where the Witnesses of them were remote, he hath now two Witnesses in the Province of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> who go along with him towards <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi>: Where shall we find him in the next Chapter.</ns0:note>
